sentences.text: Did I actually say anything true in there, or just the version of me that performs okay? My copay was thirty dollars; my silence, apparently, has been free for years. Filling out the intake form took longer than the crying did. There's a question on the paperwork that asks you to rate your hopelessness from one to ten, like it's spice level at a restaurant. I kept staring at the box of tissues on her side table, daring myself not to need it. At checkout the receptionist called me "hon" while photocopying my card, and I had to study the carpet for a second. Maybe I'll cancel, maybe I'll go; either way the appointment card keeps riding around in my coat pocket. When I finally said the ugly thing out loud, she didn't flinch, and her not flinching undid something in me. Two buses and a fifteen-minute walk each way, every single week — I keep wondering if I can actually sustain that. She asked what brought me in, and I heard myself say "nothing, really," which we both knew was a lie. Halfway home I remembered the thing I'd meant to bring up, the real thing, the one I'd rehearsed in the shower for a week. Some of it helped, I think, though I couldn't tell you which part, and that vagueness bothers me. Told my sister it was a dentist appointment; that felt easier than explaining what it actually was. Tuesday at four, she said, same time next week — and I nodded like a person who knows where I'll be next week. Three weeks until the next opening, the coordinator said, and I laughed a little, because what else. Fifty minutes, and I spent the first twenty explaining my insurance card. The parking meter outside her office only took quarters, and I sat there feeding it like the hour hadn't already cost me enough. Have I ever told anyone before, he asked, and the honest answer — no one, not once — just hung there. What do you do with your face in a waiting room where everyone knows why everyone else is there? Fragile isn't the word; scraped clean is closer to how the drive home felt. Anyone have recs for epistolary grief fics that handle a discovered letter without tipping into melodrama? Mods pinned a reminder that threads dissecting the suicide note chapter must carry spoiler tags through the weekend. I want to write a suicide letter.
